What do you mean exactly? Are you asking about comp diff between these levels or something else?

I’m asking if anyone has any clear distinguishers in signals for IC6 vs IC7, and I guess also the down leveling for IC5. Ideally the whole interview process is used for signal gathering, but seeing if I do things well in the technical screen that I can get a distributed systems design interview IC6+. Is that helpful?

Gotcha. Tagging
@CaliMan , @fx18 , @Ultra Instinct for their inputs

The differentiating factors between levels are the level of ambiguity you are able to deal with, the amount of guidance you require and the scope of the programs you able to lead.  I don't know if there is a formulaic ratio between the interviews to decide your level but if anything I'd say that your performance tech interview is a required but not sufficient to set your target level.

In other words it's the program sense, leadership, partnership interviews that set your level and the tech/solution design need to be strong enough to support it. Doing better in the tech interviews won't bump you up in level.
@AG Does this sound about right from what you know as well?
Yeah. In the end, they'll also look at overall yoe and where those years were spent to inform their decision. (Yeah, it is a halo bias, whether we like it or not) 🤷🏽‍♂️

Thank you both @AG and @CaliMan! This is a very helpful perspective. Internal understanding of company norms for leveling should play into all of that, and I deeply appreciate the insight. I understand the avoiding of formulas too as each case is unique. In the bigger picture perspective, the high level guidance helps me in framing my answers while my work yoe and companies tell another aspect of it

Back at a desk, here are my thoughts:

* In general, this seems like a good E2E program ownership example except that it reads too good to be true (i.e. it feels like you might be taking too much credit). This is a difficult balance. 
As written, this claims you handled 
1/ product justification and financial modeling of what sounds like at least a $XY MM investment, if not $XYZ MM investment
2/ technical validation of deep network issues like BGP peering while covering both Origin && Edge needs
3/ launch TPM responsibilities across this whole thing
If I had to guess, you were probably involved in all those things, but not the "main driver" for many of them. There's a difference between saying "I coordinated teams to ensure X" and "I ensured X". 

* Technical Depth vs Business Framing: I think you cover the business framing fine (10MM concurrent viewers, $35MM Revenue). I don't think that you cover the technical details enough. Examples:
1/ Separate from your story you noted that there's both pre-recorded and live content distributed on this infrastructure. Those have very different technical constraints and implementations
2/ You gloss over the detail that you apparently handled both Edge PoPs and Origin DCs that handle ingestion/encoding/transcoding. Those also have different technical constraints and implementations. (As a side note, this is a contributor for "this feels too good to be true for one IC's work")
3/ You talk about ensuring network readiness, but is that because y'all operated your own private network backbone across dark fiber? If so, that isn't explained anywhere

* Clarity: As written, the story is generally coherent and cohesive. It feels like it's missing details like those I listed above, but it goes from A to Z in a standard STAR pattern. One key detail missing is the timeframe you did this in. Was this done in a quarter? a year? 3 years? What's the order of magnitude of Origins & PoPs this required?

Hey @LeverageCoach - Thanks for taking the time to provide such detailed feedback—I really appreciate it 🙏

You’re absolutely right that I didn’t personally execute every part of the setup. The project spanned nearly two years and involved several TPMs. My intent was to present the overall scope of the initiative so it conveys why the infrastructure effort itself was significant and worth managing. 

That said, I’ll refine the narrative to focus more clearly on the specific area where I personally contributed and drove outcomes. I’ll also make sure to clarify the project timeline so the context is more accurate.

I would establish that level of ownership/contribution up front. I recommend being very explicit about what you were the "single threaded owner" of.

To underscore the impact of this discrepancy: if this exchange happened during a live interview, it would be an immediate red flag and likely disqualify you. 

The follow-up would be interpreted as the initial story being proven as overstating only because I had domain expertise to push. That means I can't trust any other responses in areas where I don't have domain expertise.

Why is this a red flag? I can coach technical skills, I can't coach integrity. 

(This isn't to say you don't have integrity, but that is how my rationale given the limited evidence would go)

I'm sure your direct involvement in this program is impressive enough.  Let it shine!
Interesting. thanks, I did not think of this perspective. Again, apprecaite the candid feedback.
